notes:
Summary:
- Goldshore is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for transaction-level inference across fraud and customer support use cases. Primary ask: contract-level throughput guarantees + strict SLA language around uptime, credits, and maintenance windows.

Key technical requirements (from infra/ML leads):
- Workload: mix of short chat + mid-sized reranking requests. Heavy peak windows (batch settlement jobs) require sustained throughput.
- Throughput targets: baseline POC target = 200 requests/sec at 512-token average; sustained burst handling up to 1.5x baseline for 15m windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for interactive chat; p99 generally acceptable up to 500ms for reranking.
- Reserved GPU planning: want 16-card reserved pool (NVIDIA A100-ish equivalent), deterministic allocation per tenant environment, options to burst to shared pool.
- Model preferences: quantized Llama-3 family + a smaller reranker variant. Must support fast kernel selection and KV-cache for conversation.

SLA negotiation specifics discussed:
- Goldshore asks for 99.99% monthly uptime. Redwood initial proposal: 99.95% with credit schedule.
- Credit schedule (current proposed language): 5% monthly service credit if uptime <99.95% but >=99.5%; 10% credit if uptime <99.5% but >=99.0%; 25% credit below 99.0%. Goldshore counters: steeper credits and pursuit of 4 9s.
- Maintenance windows: Goldshore requires no more than 4 hours/month of unannounced interruptions for production; prefer scheduled maintenance in 2x/month 1-hour windows during 02:00-05:00 local. Redwood proposes monthly 2-hour maintenance with advance notice + emergency patching rights.
- Support response SLA: P1 (service down) — 1 hour response, P2 (degraded perf) — 4 hours, P3 (non-urgent) — next business day. Goldshore wants 30-minute P1 for first 6 months of contract.

Security/compliance notes:
- Goldshore will route PCI-adjacent tokens and needs private control plane (VPC) + customer-managed KMS. SOC2 Type II report required; ISO27001 in roadmap but not mandatory. Retention controls and per-route audit logs are must-haves.

POC status & timeline:
- NDA signed 2025-11-20.
- Security questionnaire submitted (SSQ-2025-11) — SOC2 docs provided by Redwood 2026-01-05.
- POC kicked off 2026-01-18: two-week perf run completed 2026-02-01. Results: p95 latency ~185ms on dedicated single-shard config; throughput shortfall on unquantized weights.
- Follow-up tuning run with 4-bit quantization and kernel tweaks completed 2026-02-18 — met baseline throughput in 3/4 runs; need deterministic test for SLA acceptance.

Commercial/contract notes:
- Goldshore requests a clause for service credits to be applied as % of monthly committed fee, not usage.
- Wants termination rights if sustained SLA failures >3 months.
- Interested in an annual reserved capacity discount for committed GPU pool + 30-day early termination opt-out during first year.

Quotes & customer voice snippets:
- CTO (A. Moreno): "We cannot accept unpredictable maintenance during market hours — that kills settlement windows."
- Head of SRE: "Need deterministic routing & pinned GPU capacity per environment; fallback model variants ok but must be seamless."

Next steps (short):
- Draft SOW/SLA incorporating counterproposal to uptime and credits (owner: Maya) — due 2026-02-28.
- Legal alignment call scheduled 2026-03-02 (Goldshore legal + Redwood legal).
- Final procurement sign-off target: 2026-03-20.

Open questions for Redwood PD/Infra:
- Can we offer an optional 99.99% SLO with higher committed pool + financial terms? If yes, need internal pricing model and availability constraints.
- Exact maintenance cadence we can guarantee for Dedicated customers in that region.
- Bursting model: deterministic limits and expected latency impacts during bursts.
